q2: Mostly supported, but weaker than stated. Context (02:12:07-02:19:38): Emily dislikes console tabs and asks for something 'to kind of play around with'. Kobi offers ('what we can do is...') a standard app with the same objects so they can compare. Joyce says 'Excellent.' That is an accepted offer, not a scoped commitment. It has no date or owner beyond Kobi, and the Gemini 'Next steps' lists (2 versions) do not list it. On per-role apps: Joyce says 'We should do that', but Emily then says reps should be able to pick their view. Kobi then says per-role apps are 'usually things that you do once you're in the system ... not a heavy lift ... additional UX UI layer that's easy to add on' after base workflows are done. So the per-role app is a deferred, unresolved idea, not a decision to record. The Gemini summary says 'consensus was to configure distinct application views', which overstates the transcript.

Earlier related rows: L0614 (25 Jun, video comparing console vs standard) and L1645 (11 Aug, sales app removed so the console is the only app). corrections: L3333 raw transcript line is 1862, not 1819 (the claim cites 1819). L3332 at line 1812 is correct.
Treat the comparison app as an accepted offer, not a firm commitment. It is not in the Gemini next-steps action items.
Per-role apps: Kobi framed these as post-launch ('once you're in the system'), and Emily wants rep choice. Treat it as an open or deferred question, not an endorsed decision.
